sources: https://dec.ny.gov/places/moose-river-plains-complex (read via WebFetch; dec.ny.gov refuses plain curl)

values.note: Sites are 'available on a first come - first served basis and cannot be reserved.' A permit from a Forest Ranger (1-877-457-5680) is needed for stays of more than 3 nights at one location or groups of 10 or more.

booking.source: https://dec.ny.gov/places/moose-river-plains-complex ('available on a first come - first served basis and cannot be reserved'; 'A camping permit is required for groups of 10 or more or for stays of more than 3 nights at one location'), read 2026-10-21

hookups.source: https://dec.ny.gov/places/moose-river-plains-complex ('There are no hook-ups for water or electricity at campsites'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: 116 numbered primitive roadside sites along Limekiln Lake-Cedar River Road, Otter Brook Road, Rock Dam Road and short spurs; DEC: 'Tents or small campers can use designated campsites.' Eight are accessible sites (1, 7, 34, 66, 73, 90, 119a, 130). DEC states no rig length.

sites.source: https://dec.ny.gov/places/moose-river-plains-complex ('There are 116 primitive roadside campsites located along the Limekiln Lake-Cedar River Road'; 'Tents or small campers can use designated campsites'; 'Eight roadside primitive campsites (Sites: 1, 7, 34, 66, 73, 90, 119a, 130)'), read 2026-10-21. max_rig_ft 30 was note-derived from reviewer reports and DEC states no length, so it is cleared.

values.note: Most sites have a picnic table, fireplace and privy.

facilities.source: https://dec.ny.gov/places/moose-river-plains-complex ('Roadside campsites are numbered and most have a picnic table, fireplace and privy'), read 2026-10-21

note: NYSDEC primitive camping in the Moose River Plains Wild Forest between Inlet and Indian Lake: numbered roadside sites along the 23-mile gravel Limekiln Lake-Cedar River Road. Seasonal road (a snowmobile route in winter); reviewers bring 26-ft class C motorhomes and a 30-ft fifth wheel, but Class A rigs are not recommended. As of 2026-09-29 a bridge failure at Payne Brook closes the eastern end (sites 1-20, road barricaded near site 21) - enter from the Limekiln Lake/Inlet gate; DEC still posted it 2026-10-21. --Claude
summary: DEC's page confirms free, first-come (cannot be reserved), no hookups; NEW: 116 designated numbered roadside sites, 8 accessible, most with table/fireplace/privy, permit for 3+ nights or 10+ people. Cleared the reviewer-derived max_rig_ft 30 (DEC: 'Tents or small campers', no length). Payne Brook bridge closure (sites 1-20) still posted - kept in the note (partial closure, not a status). Note trimmed of fee/booking/hookup restatements. DEC states no road surface, road season or 4WD requirement.
flags: Missing phone: DEC Region 5 Northville Office 518-863-4545 (M-F 7:30-3:30), the office the page lists (trail reports ext. 3005).

Rig size: DEC says only 'Tents or small campers can use designated campsites' and gives no length; whether a 23-ft Class C counts as a 'small camper' is not stated (the 26-ft Class C reports in the note are reviewer reports). No 4WD/high-clearance requirement is posted.

Road closure: 'Due to a bridge failure at Payne Brook, the eastern segment of Limekiln Lake-Cedar River Road is closed from the Cedar River Flow Headquarters building west to Campsite 20 ... Campsites 1-20 are closed'; access only from the Limekiln Lake/Inlet entrance (DEC page, 2026-10-21).
DEC's page gives no opening/closing dates for the seasonal road, so no season is recorded.
